Games Action Games Grand Theft Auto GTA 6 After avoiding GTA 5 for 13 years, Trevor actor says he's excited for GTA 6 and might even stream it News By Jordan Gerblick Published 15 October 2026 Steven Ogg is coming home When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works . (Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Steven Ogg, the actor best known for playing Trevor in GTA 5, spent many years pretending the game didn't exist, but 13 years later, he's fully embracing his role in making it so special. For a few weeks now, Ogg has been participating in a series of GTA 5 livestreams hosted by his co-star, Michael actor Ned Luke, and in the latest episode, Ogg not only acknowledges GTA 6 's existence - he expresses vague excitement for the sequel and even floats the idea of streaming it alongside Luke. Progress. This is a huge flip from February 2025, when Ogg denied the common perception that he "hates" GTA but maintained that he wouldn't be playing GTA 6 . It seems Ogg has had a change of heart, as he sounds much more enthusiastic about Rockstar's upcoming behemoth these days. "We should also do this with the new one, when the GTA 6 comes out," Ogg tells Luke, immediately reminding everyone he doesn't play games by referring to it as the GTA 6. "Because, obviously, it's gonna be so fucking different, and talking about the animation, and... it'd be kind of fun." Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: The Final Mission Episode 11: Sunshine, Boredom, Lies (feat. Steven Ogg) - YouTube Watch On Luke definitely agrees with Ogg's idea, telling him he plans to finish his playthrough of GTA 5 before GTA 6 comes out on November 19, clearing the way for a smooth transition into streaming the next game. In a fascinating exchange, Ogg asks Luke if he's "in touch with... them," seemingly referring to Rockstar, and Luke, seemingly caught off guard, pauses before saying "no," and laughing nervously as Ogg spins around in his chair mischievously. "You're like one of the guys at the Comic-Cons, man" Luke says. "Well, I can tell you but then I'd have to kill you." Ogg then continues about his interest in GTA 6, saying he's "curious about the actors .. and the game itself, those characters, versus this, GTA 5, which obviously I learn more and more about over the 12 years." You may like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption actor auditioned for over 60 roles in GTA 6 and never heard back Parts of GTA 6 are "a bit outdated and weird," says former Rockstar dev Rockstar reportedly reminded GTA 6's voice cast they're still under NDA Admittedly, it's unclear from Ogg's tone and general vagueness of speech whether he's genuinely excited for GTA 6 or if he's just shooting the shit with an old friend and colleague, but either way, this is a huge step forward from when he was seemingly ignoring the series' existence altogether.
